description: Agent Capacity: submit an agent’s backlog records across a window: the window with its start and end dates; each backlog item with its id, what it is, when it opened, when it closed and when it last saw activity; optionally the days with no activity after which an open item counts as abandoned in place (30 when left out); and the oldest an open item should be, in days. The signed report gives the window, the backlog open at its start and at its end with the change, the direction (growing, steady or shrinking) and the items opened and closed between them, every item open at the end with its age and its days since last activity, the oldest item waiting with its age and the median age, and every item abandoned in place with its last activity and days idle, and counts them, and names a growing backlog: more open items at the end of the window than at its start, and open items with no activity past the abandonment window; then a backlog held level rather than worked down, and open items older than the age limit, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No window, no items, no age limit or open items with no recorded last activity leave the backlog unverified. This reads a backlog’s size and age across a window from its item records: whether waiting items are re-reviewed at their review point is wever_triage-aging-check, how each item left the queue is wever_triage-disposition-check and a report’s queue figures against its records are wever_triage-report-check. Verdict capacity_backlog_growing, capacity_backlog_partial, capacity_backlog_unverified or capacity_backlog_shrinking. POST /api/capacity-backlog-check. Reads the load and capacity records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Capacity reads an agent’s own load and capacity records and checks the load against the capacity that exists: work in hand against the stated limit, a queue against its target wait, concurrent runs against the cap, an allowance’s burn against its period, a backlog across a window, spare capacity against the reserve, the scaling plan against the burn, and admission at capacity against written priority rules. Beside it, the Agent Limits checks such as wever_limit-substrate-check read whether a limit sits in code or in prose and how it is scoped, changed and seen, while a capacity check reads the load itself against the capacity; wever_commitment-deadline-check reads promised hours against due dates, while the workload check reads the work in hand against the stated limit over time; and the Agent Triage checks such as wever_triage-priority-check read how queue items are ranked, reviewed and closed, while the queue, backlog and throttle checks read waits, size and admission against capacity. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-capacity-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-capacity/.
